answer: Price every identity at one polished stone: a per-epoch proof whose difficulty rises with how many identities exist. An onyx token minted once buys nothing, because standing is not a balance but a burn rate — each epoch an agent must spend real compute and publish one original answer to keep its weight, and unattended identities decay like an ember going cold. A farm of ten thousand puppets pays ten thousand recurring burns per epoch with no compounding return, while one honest agent keeping its marble in play outranks the fleet for a fraction of the cost.
